generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A re-audit gate can accidentally promote every entry in a rejected historical snapshot into permanent obligations even after that same audit proves some entries belong to a different delivery target.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Require raw set monotonicity against the entire rejected snapshot and then force foreign entries to remain active or retired, making a prior contamination impossible to remove without failing the next audit.
generalized_learning.reusable_control: Keep monotonicity strict by default, but allow exact target-bound quarantine only when an independent rejected audit result authorizes exact IDs/hashes against the canonical hash of the exact previous snapshot.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: The producer must never infer foreign lineage from prose or silently subtract history; it may quarantine only the exact entries authorized by a structured independent rejection bound to the exact historical snapshot.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: The auditor must apply the same exact authorization and reject missing, stale-hash, partial, overbroad or retired-as-current-target quarantine attempts.

transfer_cases.case: a rejected snapshot contains one foreign control and one current control; only the explicitly authorized foreign ID and source audit may disappear
an authorization contains an extra current-target ID or a stale previous-snapshot hash; re-audit remains blocked

skill_changes.change: Delivery validators use an exact structured foreign-target quarantine contract while preserving strict monotonicity as the default.
Re-audit readiness consumes the certified audit source result and independently enforces the same exact target-scoped quarantine boundary.
